```{r}
read_table <- function(filename) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(tables_dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

read_main_table <- function(filename) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(main_tables_dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

read_repeatability <- function(filename) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(repeatability_dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

p_text <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "—",
    p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
    TRUE ~ sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), p)
  )
}

p_report <- function(p) {
  if_else(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", p_text(p)))
}

range_text <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("%.", digits, "f–%.", digits, "f"),
    min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

# Convert internal or legacy morph codes to complete manuscript labels.
morph_label <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)

  x |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(
      stringr::regex(
        "\\b(?:8th|8|eight|eighth)(?:[-\\s]+instar)?\\b",
        ignore_case = TRUE
      ),
      "Eighth instar"
    ) |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(
      stringr::regex(
        "\\b(?:9th|9|nine|ninth)(?:[-\\s]+instar)?\\b",
        ignore_case = TRUE
      ),
      "Ninth instar"
    ) |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(
      stringr::regex(
        "\\b(?:10th|10|ten|tenth)(?:[-\\s]+instar)?\\b",
        ignore_case = TRUE
      ),
      "Tenth instar"
    ) |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(
      stringr::regex("\\bfemale(?:s)?\\b", ignore_case = TRUE),
      "Female"
    )
}

supplementary_table <- function(x, align = NULL, font_size = 8.5) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  rule <- officer::fp_border(color = "#000000", width = 0.75)

  ft <- flextable::flextable(x) |>
    flextable::font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = font_size, part = "all") |>
    flextable::color(color = "#000000", part = "all") |>
    flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
    flextable::border_remove() |>
    flextable::hline_top(border = rule, part = "header") |>
    flextable::hline_bottom(border = rule, part = "header") |>
    flextable::padding(padding = 2, part = "all") |>
    flextable::valign(valign = "center", part = "all") |>
    flextable::autofit() |>
    flextable::set_table_properties(
      layout = "autofit",
      width = 1,
      opts_word = list(split = FALSE)
    )

  if (!is.null(align)) {
    for (j in seq_along(align)) {
      ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = j, align = align[[j]], part = "all")
    }
  }

  ft
}

# Measurement reliability -----------------------------------------------------
repeatability_all <- read_repeatability("measurement_repeatability_robustness.csv")
round_effects     <- read_repeatability("measurement_round_effects.csv")
round_pairwise    <- read_repeatability("measurement_round_pairwise_diagnostics.csv")
order_effects     <- read_repeatability("measurement_order_effects.csv")

repeatability_primary <- repeatability_all |>
  filter(model == "primary_unadjusted")
repeatability_morph <- repeatability_all |>
  filter(model == "morph_adjusted")
repeatability_round <- repeatability_all |>
  filter(model == "morph_and_round_adjusted")

trait_labels <- c(
  pronotum = "Pronotum length",
  head_length = "Head length",
  head_width = "Head width",
  forefemur = "Forefemur length",
  foretibia = "Foretibia length",
  midfemur = "Midfemur length",
  midtibia = "Midtibia length",
  hindfemur = "Hindfemur length",
  hindtibia = "Hindtibia length",
  ear = "Ear area",
  eye = "Eye length"
)

trait_order <- names(trait_labels)

repeatability_display <- repeatability_primary |>
  select(trait, pooled_R = R, pooled_lower = CI_lower, pooled_upper = CI_upper) |>
  left_join(
    repeatability_morph |>
      select(trait, morph_R = R, morph_lower = CI_lower, morph_upper = CI_upper),
    by = "trait"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    repeatability_round |>
      select(
        trait,
        round_R = R,
        round_lower = CI_lower,
        round_upper = CI_upper
      ),
    by = "trait"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    round_effects |>
      select(
        trait,
        relative_TEM_percent,
        absolute_agreement_ICC_A1,
        max_absolute_pairwise_bias_percent,
        round_P_Holm
      ),
    by = "trait"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    trait = factor(trait, levels = trait_order),
    Trait = unname(trait_labels[as.character(trait)]),
    Pooled = sprintf("%.4f\n(%.4f–%.4f)", pooled_R, pooled_lower, pooled_upper),
    `Morph-adjusted` = sprintf(
      "%.4f\n(%.4f–%.4f)", morph_R, morph_lower, morph_upper
    ),
    `Morph + round` = sprintf(
      "%.4f\n(%.4f–%.4f)", round_R, round_lower, round_upper
    ),
    `rTEM (%)` = sprintf("%.2f", relative_TEM_percent),
    `ICC(A,1)` = sprintf("%.4f", absolute_agreement_ICC_A1),
    `Max. bias (%)` = sprintf("%.2f", max_absolute_pairwise_bias_percent),
    `Holm p` = p_text(round_P_Holm)
  ) |>
  arrange(trait) |>
  select(
    Trait,
    Pooled,
    `Morph-adjusted`,
    `Morph + round`,
    `rTEM (%)`,
    `ICC(A,1)`,
    `Max. bias (%)`,
    `Holm p`
  )

min_signed_order_q   <- min(order_effects$signed_slope_P_BH, na.rm = TRUE)
min_absolute_order_q <- min(order_effects$absolute_error_slope_P_BH, na.rm = TRUE)

# Dimensionality sensitivities ------------------------------------------------
rank_one <- read_table("female_reference_rank_one_tests.csv")
classification_rank <- read_table("group_divergence_classification_sensitivity.csv") |>
  filter(excluded > 0)
pca_primary <- read_table("pca_parallel_analysis.csv") |> filter(component == "PC1")

  filter(component == "PC1")

  filter(component == "PC1")

rank_primary <- rank_one |> filter(scenario == "standardized_head_excluded")
rank_six     <- rank_one |> filter(scenario == "standardized_six")
rank_raw     <- rank_one |> filter(scenario == "raw_log_six")

dimensionality_display <- bind_rows(
  rank_one |>
    transmute(
      Approach = "Female-referenced rank-one test",
      Scenario = recode(
        scenario,
        standardized_head_excluded = "Five traits, standardized; head excluded (base scenario)",
        standardized_six = "Six traits, standardized; head included",
        raw_log_six = "Six traits on raw log scale"
      ),
      Estimate = sprintf("%.1f%% captured by rank one", 100 * rank_one_fraction),
      `Null reference` = sprintf("Residual share: 95th percentile = %.1f%%", 100 * null_95),
      `p-value` = p_text(p_value),
      Conclusion = if_else(p_value < 0.05, "Departure from rank one detected", "No departure detected")
    ),
  classification_rank |>
    transmute(
      Approach = "Female-referenced rank-one test",
      Scenario = "Five traits after excluding category disagreements",
      Estimate = sprintf("%.1f%% captured by rank one", 100 * rank_one_fraction),
      `Null reference` = sprintf("Residual share: 95th percentile = %.1f%%", 100 * null_95),
      `p-value` = p_text(p_value),
      Conclusion = if_else(p_value < 0.05, "Departure from rank one detected", "No departure detected")
    ),
  bind_rows(
    pca_primary |> mutate(Scenario = "Five traits, standardized; head excluded (base scenario)"),
    pca_six |> mutate(Scenario = "Six traits, standardized; head included"),
    pca_classification |>
      mutate(Scenario = "Five traits after excluding classification-sensitive males")
  ) |>
    transmute(
      Approach = "PCA with parallel analysis",
      Scenario,
      Estimate = sprintf(
        "PC1 = %.1f%%; eigenvalue %.3f",
        variance_percent,
        observed_eigenvalue
      ),
      `Null reference` = sprintf(
        "95th-percentile eigenvalue = %.3f",
        parallel_95_eigenvalue
      ),
      `p-value` = "—",
      Conclusion = "One component retained"
    )
)

    `Numerator df` = numerator_df,
    `Residual df` = residual_df,
    F = round(F, 2),
    `p-value` = p_text(p_value)
  )

eye_head_support_display <- eye_head_support |>
  transmute(
    Group = group,
    n,
    `Minimum head size` = round(minimum_head_size, 3),
    `Maximum head size` = round(maximum_head_size, 3),
    `Common lower bound` = round(common_lower, 3),
    `Common upper bound` = round(common_upper, 3),
    `Common support` = if_else(common_overlap, "Yes", "No")
  )

# Equivalence-region sensitivity ---------------------------------------------
leg_equivalence <- read_table("leg_intermediacy_equivalence.csv")
sensory_equivalence <- read_table("sensory_intermediacy_equivalence.csv")

equivalence_sensitivity_display <- bind_rows(
  leg_equivalence |>
    transmute(
      Trait = leg,
      Scale = "Length ratio",
      `Equivalence region` = paste0("±", equivalence_margin_percent, "%"),
      Ratio = estimate_ratio,
      `Lower 90% CI` = lower_90_ratio,
      `Upper 90% CI` = upper_90_ratio,
      TOST_p,
      equivalent
    ),
  sensory_equivalence |>
    transmute(
      Trait = trait,
      Scale = reported_scale,
      `Equivalence region` = paste0("±", equivalence_margin_percent, "%"),
      Ratio = estimate_ratio,
      `Lower 90% CI` = lower_90_ratio,
      `Upper 90% CI` = upper_90_ratio,
      TOST_p,
      equivalent
    )
) |>
  transmute(
    Trait,
    Scale,
    `Equivalence region`,
    Ratio = round(Ratio, 3),
    `Lower 90% CI` = round(`Lower 90% CI`, 3),
    `Upper 90% CI` = round(`Upper 90% CI`, 3),
    `TOST p` = p_text(TOST_p),
    Equivalent = if_else(equivalent, "Yes", "No")
  )

# Cross-analysis multiplicity sensitivity ------------------------------------
focal_multiplicity <- read_table("focal_multiplicity_sensitivity.csv")

focal_multiplicity_display <- focal_multiplicity |>
  transmute(
    Analysis = analysis,
    Tier = tier,
    `Raw p` = p_text(p_value),
    `BH p` = p_text(p_BH),
    `Holm p` = p_text(p_Holm)
  )

# Detailed estimates for the analyses described in the main manuscript ------
leg_contrasts_main <- read_main_table("joint_leg_males_vs_female.csv")
leg_slopes_main <- read_main_table("joint_leg_slopes.csv")
segment_tests_main <- read_main_table("segment_slope_model_tests.csv")
ear_means_main <- read_main_table("ear_body_adjusted_group_means.csv")
eye_means_main <- read_main_table("eye_body_adjusted_group_means.csv")

leg_contrasts_main_display <- leg_contrasts_main |>
  transmute(
    Leg = leg,
    Contrast = contrast,
    `Difference (%)` = round(percent_difference, 1),
    `Ratio lower 95% CI` = round(ratio_lower, 3),
    `Ratio upper 95% CI` = round(ratio_upper, 3),
    `Adjusted p` = p_text(p.value)
  )

leg_slopes_main_display <- leg_slopes_main |>
  transmute(
    Group = group, Leg = leg,
    Slope = round(`logP_c.trend`, 3),
    `Lower 95% CI` = round(lower.CL, 3),
    `Upper 95% CI` = round(upper.CL, 3)
  )

segment_tests_main_display <- segment_tests_main |>
  transmute(
    Segment = analysis,
    `Numerator df` = numerator_df,
    `Residual df` = full_residual_df,
    F = round(F, 2),
    `p-value` = p_text(p_value)
  )

sensory_means_main_display <- bind_rows(
  ear_means_main |>
    transmute(
      Trait = "Tympanic organ area (mm²)", Group = group,
      Estimate = predicted_ear_area,
      `Lower 95% CI` = ear_area_lower,
      `Upper 95% CI` = ear_area_upper
    ),
  eye_means_main |>
    transmute(
      Trait = "Eye length (mm)", Group = group,
      Estimate = predicted_eye_length,
      `Lower 95% CI` = eye_lower,
      `Upper 95% CI` = eye_upper
    )
) |>
  mutate(across(c(Estimate, `Lower 95% CI`, `Upper 95% CI`), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

# Overview

This supplement provides measurement-reliability results and detailed weapon–trait and sensory estimates (Tables S1–S6), multivariate and robustness analyses (Tables S7–S13), and additional estimates from the leg and sensory models (Tables S14–S17). Tables S18–S19 summarize within-group correlations and the precision of planned leg contrasts. Figures S1–S4 show within-group correlations, individual-level ordination, body-size distributions and leg allometries.

The distinction between the five-trait reference analysis and head-inclusive sensitivities identifies the trait sets, not their confirmatory status. Dimensionality, matrix comparisons, equivalence-region checks and the cross-analysis multiplicity audit are exploratory. Both documents use the same analysis outputs and retain the original morph assignments. Reproduction instructions and additional model outputs are supplied with the analysis code.

# Supplementary methods

## Measurement reliability

Forty-eight specimens from the 2016 collection were measured on three occasions. The measurement-order file records 12 individuals per sex or morph group and one from each of 12 size strata within each group. Repeatability was estimated for pooled, morph-adjusted and morph-plus-round models. Relative technical error of measurement, absolute-agreement ICC(A,1), round-pair bias and measurement-order trends were also calculated. The order analyses were treated as diagnostics; their minimum Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p-values were `r p_text(min_signed_order_q)` for signed drift and `r p_text(min_absolute_order_q)` for absolute-error drift.

## Multivariate sensitivity analyses

The reference female-referenced contrast-vector and PCA analyses excluded composite head size because head length contributed to male morph assignment. Each log trait was standardized by its residual standard deviation from a pooled regression on log pronotum length. Sensitivities restored head size and repeated the six-trait rank-one decomposition on unstandardized log measurements. Rank-one tests used `r rank_primary$permutations` residual randomizations; the matrix tests used `r primary_covariance$permutations` randomizations.

Pairwise directional comparisons constrained two male–female contrast vectors to share a direction while leaving the third unconstrained. The angle between each pair was compared with its pair-specific rank-one randomization distribution, with Holm adjustment across the three pairs. Group-stratified bootstrap samples provided percentile 95% intervals for vector angles and differences in magnitude (Table S2).

Morph assignments were based on head-length categories derived from mixture models in @kelly2010 and @kelly2026, rather than models fitted to this sample. Archived assignments correspond to boundaries of approximately 18.51 and 24.15 mm; the exact cut-offs used to reconstruct them are 18.50579 and 24.15225 mm. The 2010 boundaries of 19.04 and 24.20 mm provide an alternative category definition. I excluded males whose labels differed between these definitions and repeated the five-trait rank-one analysis, recalculating standardization and group-specific size adjustments. The same exclusion was assessed for the individual-level PCA and head-adjusted eye model. These checks assess dependence on category boundaries, not the accuracy of individual developmental histories.

## Matrix comparisons and unequal sample sizes

Within-group covariance and correlation matrices for the five non-head traits were compared using omnibus and pairwise Frobenius-distance randomization tests. Pairwise p-values were adjusted by both Benjamini–Hochberg and Holm procedures. Matrix-element correlations and random-skewers similarities were used as descriptive orientation measures. To evaluate unequal group sizes, each group was repeatedly rarefied to 38 specimens, the size of the tenth-instar male group.

## Repeated-leg covariance structure

The main repeated-leg model estimated separate residual variances for fore-, mid- and hindlegs and freely estimated the three within-individual residual correlations. It was compared with compound-symmetry and heterogeneous compound-symmetry structures using fits with identical fixed effects. The selected unstructured model is used for main-text inference and the associated precision calculations.

## Secondary integration, equivalence and sampling checks

Main-text weapon–leg relationships were estimated in one stage from raw log composite head size while controlling for pronotum length, group and leg identity. Weapon–ear slopes were likewise estimated in one stage; an exploratory equivalence sensitivity assessed them against an illustrative standardized near-zero region of −0.20 to 0.20. All-pairs sensory tests were Holm-adjusted within each six-comparison trait family and are separate from the main text's planned contrast families. For Holm-tested contrasts, simultaneous 95% confidence intervals use Bonferroni adjustment over the stated family; slope and predicted-mean intervals are pointwise. The separate precision estimates use pointwise intervals and approximate minimum detectable effects for a single two-sided test at 80% power and $\alpha=0.05$. They do not include a correction for testing several contrasts. Morph-composition χ² tests compared the analysed males with two published empirical compositions; they diagnose compositional mismatch but cannot identify its cause because collection microhabitat and gallery-search effort were not retained.

## Cross-analysis multiplicity audit

The within-family Holm adjustments reported for planned contrasts remain the manuscript's inferential corrections. As a separate sensitivity analysis, ten selected omnibus p-values were adjusted together using Benjamini–Hochberg and Holm procedures. This broader audit is descriptive and does not replace the main-text tests.

# Supplementary results

## Reliability and measurement-session effects

All traits were highly repeatable, including after adjustment for morph and measurement round (Table S1). Round effects were detectable for several traits, but their magnitude was small relative to among-individual variation. No evidence of progressive signed or absolute-error drift was detected within remeasurement sessions.

## Directional dimensionality

The base five-trait rank-one model captured `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * rank_primary$rank_one_fraction)`% of design-weighted group-effect variation, while the standardized six-trait and raw-log six-trait sensitivities captured `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * rank_six$rank_one_fraction)`% and `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * rank_raw$rank_one_fraction)`%, respectively. In every case the residual component beyond rank one exceeded the randomization distribution (`r p_report(max(rank_one$p_value))`; Table S7). Excluding `r classification_rank$excluded` category-disagreement males retained `r classification_rank$n` complete cases and a rank-one share of `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * classification_rank$rank_one_fraction)`%, with a detectable residual beyond rank one (`r p_report(classification_rank$p_value)`). Parallel analysis retained one component in the reference five-trait analysis, the six-trait sensitivity and the classification-exclusion sensitivity (Supplementary Figure S2). These exploratory results show one dominant dimension together with a smaller detected secondary direction in adjusted group means.

## Matrix structure

The base five-trait omnibus tests detected neither a covariance-matrix difference (`r p_report(primary_covariance$p_value)`) nor a correlation-matrix difference (`r p_report(primary_correlation$p_value)`; Supplementary Figure S1). The six-trait sensitivity, which restores head size, detected a covariance-matrix difference (`r p_report(six_covariance$p_value)`), but not a correlation-matrix difference (`r p_report(six_correlation$p_value)`). Thus the five-trait null result cannot be generalized to all measured traits; neither nonsignificant test establishes matrix equivalence. No five-trait pairwise matrix comparison survived Holm adjustment (Table S8). Matrix-element correlations, random-skewers similarities and rarefaction summaries are reported in Table S9 rather than interpreted as independent hypothesis tests.

## Repeated-leg covariance and secondary analyses

In the alternative covariance-structure fits, unstructured repeated-leg covariance was preferred to heterogeneous compound symmetry (likelihood-ratio statistic = `r sprintf("%.2f", leg_covariance_selected$L.Ratio)`, `r p_report(leg_covariance_selected_p)`; Table S10a). Pairwise residual correlations ranged from `r sprintf("%.3f", min(leg_covariance_parameters$estimate[1:3]))` to `r sprintf("%.3f", max(leg_covariance_parameters$estimate[1:3]))` (Table S10b). All 12 one-stage raw-head weapon–leg slope estimates were positive, with 95% confidence intervals excluding zero for 11; planned differences among slopes were imprecise (Tables S3–S4). Weapon–ear slopes did not meet the illustrative equivalence criterion in any group (Table S5).

## Classification and sample composition

The archived file contained `r morph_classification$male_n` males. The published 2010 thresholds disagreed with `r morph_classification$n_disagree_legacy_2010` archived labels (`r sprintf("%.1f", morph_classification$percent_disagree_legacy_2010)`%). Excluding those specimens did not alter the head-adjusted eye-length omnibus conclusion (Table S11). Male composition differed from both published empirical references (Table S11), but the source of the difference cannot be resolved from the archive. The 7.2-mm reference pronotum used for adjusted comparisons fell within the observed range of every group (Supplementary Figure S3).

## Cross-analysis multiplicity

In the selected unstructured model, the group-by-leg allocation effect and the raw-head weapon–leg interaction remained supported in the ten-test audit. The body-size-by-group-by-leg interaction was unsupported before cross-analysis adjustment. The body-size-by-group term was supported within its model but did not survive the broader ten-test audit (Table S12), reinforcing the exploratory status of detailed allometric comparisons.

*Note.* Repeatability values are individual-level ICCs with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. rTEM is the within-individual standard deviation divided by the trait mean × 100.
